interpretation: Specific reproduced failure fingerprints, not a complete labeled accuracy dataset. Tolerance identifies the old failure neighborhood, not an event-error bound. Media are private and remain outside Git.

cases.evidence: A native-refinement development candidate accepted a colored patch at 8.800 s although another cue 0.233 s later failed a full-frame camera-cut check. The source frame shows athletes already launching and no timing lamp at the selected patch. Nearby visual cues cannot independently bypass a failed global scene check.

A native-refinement development candidate accepted a colored area during a tight athlete/LED-banner shot at 7.800 s. A neighboring cue at 8.000 s detected a major camera cut. The pre/post-reframe motion cannot establish a continuous launch from that proposed clock.

A development candidate recovered the real start light, then used a Low-confidence window-reflection fallback to accept Finish at 31.433 s, long after the climb was complete. Weak patches must not replace stronger verified lane evidence during Finish search.

Audio-only analysis labeled a 553.8/601.3/1064.3 Hz sequence High at 7.14 s, after the lane B timer visibly stopped at 5.99 s. The full app's launch guard withheld acceptance. This timestamp must never be automatically accepted as race start.
A red-dominant obstruction was accepted as the lower sensor's green return while the athlete was still climbing.
A late upper timing-unit reset was corroborated by a foreground person's apparent top-band movement. The timer was already stopped earlier in the clip.
